Instead of doing her job and verifying the advertised price, she ordered me to go downstairs, take a picture of the sign, and bring it back to her. I told her that checking the advertised price was the store’s responsibility, not the customer’s. Another employee eventually went to verify the price.

Rather than assisting a customer, the cashier became aggressive, hostile, and completely unprofessional. She repeatedly shouted “Kiss my ass!” loud enough for customers throughout the store to hear. I have never experienced such disrespect from a retail employee.

No customer should ever be spoken to in this manner. An employee who tells customers to “kiss my ass” should not be serving the public. Her behavior was completely inappropriate, abusive, and far below any acceptable standard of customer service.

What made the situation even worse was that a manager was standing nearby, witnessed the incident, and failed to intervene or stop the cashier’s behavior. Instead of protecting a customer from verbal abuse, management allowed it to continue.

After the incident, I went downstairs myself. By the time I got there, the promotional signs for those drinks were no longer displayed, and I had to choose different drinks instead.

I demand that you immediately preserve and review all surveillance footage from the checkout area and the beverage section between approximately 2:00 PM and 2:30 PM on July 7, 2026. I also request a full investigation into the cashier’s conduct, the manager’s failure to act, and the handling of the advertised pricing.

I expect a written response explaining the outcome of your investigation and the corrective actions that will be taken. If this matter is not handled appropriately, I reserve the right to file complaints with the appropriate consumer protection authorities and to explore any other legal remedies that may be available.

docs.text: Google review of Jubilee Marketplace (5 out of 5, by LeGrod, 10 months ago): Popped in here while looking for something easy to have for lunch, and what a surprise it was! Great spread of food options, we tried a little bit of almost everything, and were very happy with all of it. Price was pretty good especially at the $9.99 a pound, but be prepared to run out of space in your container trying to grab some of it all. docs.title: Review of Stage Door Delicatessen
docs.text: Google review of Stage Door Delicatessen (5 out of 5, by Jenna North, 3 months ago): My daughter and I looked for some breakfast places in FiDi.  I had ate at the pizzeria upstairs but not the deli.  We decided on this deli because the menu was so full.   A lot of the places in the area have some breakfast items but not a full menu. The food was fantastic.  We were floored that the strawberry cream cheese had actual strawberries.  Eggs were perfectly over medium. The potatoes reminded me of the ones my dad used to make when I was growing up! Such nostalgia! The place wasn’t super busy.  We ordered, walked to register to pay, and food was ready.  Great prices. The service was impeccable.  Everyone was super friendly and personable.  Made us feel like friends and not just customers. Well worth a visit for good food, great prices and friendly service!

Now my go-to spot for a healthy and delicious meal that hit the spot that won’t break the bank.

docs.text: Google review of Open Market (5 out of 5, by Dane, 7 years ago): You’ve got everything you could ever hope for in his place... tacos, stir fry, sushi, burgers, a salad bar, soups, ramen.. a buffet style bar.. I mean you name it they’ve got it. Sure it gets very crowded around lunch time but that’s to be expected at a place like this and the lines move very quickly. Never have more than a 10 minute wait. The prices are on the higher side of things but I don’t mind too much since everything is fresh and often prepared right in front of you. Plenty of space of dine inside or outside if you please. The place is well lit and clean and staff is friendly and helpful. Probably my number one go to lunch spot. Thanks Open Market... see you soon!

docs.text: Google review of Leo's Bagels (5 out of 5, by Megan Ferguson, 6 months ago): Today was my first visit to Leo’s Bagels, and everyone was very helpful. I was looking at the menu on the wall and an employee offered me a paper version of the menu so I didn’t have to squint up at the wall to decide what to order. At 12:30pm on Easter Sunday, there was a very short line, and I got in and out pretty quickly (~5-7 min). The employee at the register was very helpful and polite also. I ordered the egg sandwich on an everything bagel toasted with mozzarella cheese, and the melted cheese was very nice. The everything bagel had really good flavor and texture. I also ordered the cinnamon raisin bagel toasted with plain cream cheese, it was delicious. They were very generous with the amount of cream cheese, so I ended up removing some of it. I tried both a savory and a sweet option to get a better idea of their range of options. Both the savory and sweet were good. I’m glad I grabbed extra napkins, because it was a little messy to eat. I spent about $15 total (before tip) for a breakfast sandwich + bagel with cream cheese, which seemed more reasonably priced than other breakfast options in NYC. There’s not much seating in the shop, just a small bartop facing the street (about 8-10 barstools total), so I walked across the street to the Starbucks on Pearl St. and ate at a table inside, which worked well during the heavy rain today (I didn’t want to eat at a park in the rain). Next time I’m in the city, I’ll return to Leo’s for quality bagels.

Google review of Liberty Bagels Wall Street (5 out of 5, by Rose Deliu, 6 months ago): Library Bagel absolutely blew me away — this place deserves every bit of a 5-star review.

First off, the chicken tenders… wow. These were hands down the most delicious tenders I’ve ever had. Each piece was thick, juicy, and clearly made with high-quality chicken — not those thin, dry strips you get elsewhere. The breading had the perfect crunch: crispy, golden, and seasoned just right, without overpowering the flavor of the meat. Every bite had that satisfying crunch followed by tender, flavorful chicken that practically melted in your mouth.

And then there’s the rainbow bagel with birthday cake cream cheese — easily one of the most fun and delicious things I’ve eaten in a long time. The bagel itself was soft, fresh, and subtly sweet, but once you add that birthday cake cream cheese, it turns into a full-on flavor explosion. It’s rich, creamy, and packed with that nostalgic cake batter sweetness, with little bursts of flavor in every bite. Somehow it’s indulgent without being overwhelming — just pure happiness in food form.

Between the insanely good chicken tenders and that unforgettable rainbow bagel combo, Library Bagel has completely won me over. I’ll be thinking about this meal for a long time and definitely coming back for more the next time I travel to New York.

*No photo of the bagel - my teenage daughter devoured it, before I could get a photo.

Google review of Ess-a-Bagel (5 out of 5, by Henry, a month ago): Ess-a-Bagel in the Wall Street area is a great spot for a quintessential New York bagel. The space is surprisingly large, bright, and clean, with plenty of room to sit and enjoy your food.

Service was absolutely on point. Everyone was friendly, efficient, and helpful. You really couldn’t ask for better customer service.

I kept it classic with an everything bagel, toasted with cream cheese, and a coffee. The bagel was exactly what you want from a New York bagel. Fresh, substantial, chewy, and delicious. Nothing complicated, just a really good bagel done right.

I went on a Sunday and lucked out because there was no line, although I could already see plenty of people heading in as I was leaving. I can definitely imagine this place getting busy.

If you’re in the Wall Street area and looking for a great New York bagel, this is the spot. Great food, great service, and a really nice space. Highly recommend.

Google review of Joe’s Pizza (4 out of 5, by CeeCee’s Little Journey, 3 months ago): Even though I was already full, I couldn’t skip Joe’s Pizza, one of the city’s famous spots. I decided to order just one slice to try. The staff recommended the classic cheese flavor, so I went with that.

The slice was quite nice actually, with thin crust, simple, and satisfying.
It’s the kind of classic pizza that never goes wrong.
On the table, they had cheese, chili flakes, and garlic powder for extra flavor, which making thoughtful for customer to add on based on preference.

docs.text: Google review of Joe’s Pizza (5 out of 5, by Suhrob Nuriddinov, 3 months ago): Joe’s Pizza on Fulton Street is exactly what New York pizza should be. Thin, crispy crust, perfectly balanced sauce, and that classic mozzarella stretch that makes every bite satisfying. I stopped in for a quick slice and ended up wishing I had ordered more. The pizza was served fresh, hot, and packed with flavor. The crust had just the right amount of crunch while still being soft and foldable -the true New York way. The ingredients tasted fresh, and you can tell why Joe’s has earned such a strong reputation over the years. The staff was friendly, the service was quick, and the atmosphere had that authentic no-frills NYC pizza vibe that both locals and visitors appreciate. If you’re anywhere near the Financial District and craving real New York pizza, Joe’s Pizza is absolutely worth the stop. One of the best slices in Manhattan, hands down. Highly recommended!

Google review of Fraunces Tavern (2 out of 5, by Kenya, 2 months ago): (Long review) I recently visited Fraunces Tavern, and the building itself is absolutely beautiful. It’s full of history and has a fascinating story behind it, which made the experience unique. A big part of my visit was to celebrate my husband’s birthday.

Unfortunately, the food did not meet my expectations, especially considering the prices. The dishes looked delicious when they arrived, but the food was literally as cold as the dining area. The flavor was lacking, and the temperature was a major disappointment. We ordered the mac and cheese, and the cheese wasn’t even melted, it was literally sitting on top of the dish.

The service was okay. Our waitress seemed busy, but the restaurant and museum are located in a very busy area and appear to have a steady flow of customers, so that was understandable.

We did finish our meals and didn’t complain at the time because we didn’t want to make an issue of it. The portions were generous, which was a positive. Overall, I’m glad I got to experience the historic atmosphere and see the restaurant/museum, but I wouldn’t return for the food. It’s definitely worth visiting for the history and the visuals, but my dining experience was disappointing.

Google review of Fraunces Tavern (5 out of 5, by David Green, 2 months ago): If you are looking for an unforgettable night out in New York City that perfectly blends deep American roots with an incredible contemporary vibe, look no further than the historic Fraunces Tavern on a Saturday night.

Stepping into this legendary establishment feels like taking a direct journey back to the late 1700s, but the energy inside is entirely vibrant, welcoming, and alive. We visited this past weekend and wound up celebrating a birthday with a group of three incredible women, and to lean fully into the atmosphere of the venue, they donned colonial-style wigs to look exactly like the founding fathers. It was an absolute hit. Please see pic!

The atmospheric, historic charm of the building paired beautifully with our playful tribute to George Washington’s old stomping grounds.The highlight of the evening was undoubtedly the live music. From 8:00 PM to 11:00 PM, the immensely talented Hannah Ray Teal, in a duo with her talented guitarist Will, took the stage, delivering a captivating performance. Her soulful vocals and fantastic guitar playing filled the room, providing the perfect soundtrack for an exceptional night.

Matching the stellar entertainment was the top-tier hospitality. The staff members were incredibly friendly, fast, and attentive, providing professional service throughout the entire evening. The crowd itself added another wonderful layer to the experience; the tavern attracts a fascinating, diverse mix of international patrons, making for great conversations and a global, upscale energy. Fraunces Tavern delivers on every front—history, exceptional live music, and a crowd that knows how to have a great time. It is the ultimate spot for a legendary NYC night out.

I explained that I was having difficulty and just wanted to pay cash for my order (I had the exact amount, $1.62), but instead of helping, she pointed to the work behind her and said she had too much to do.

Google review of Chick-fil-A (5 out of 5, by Department of Place Ratings, 6 months ago): Chick-fil-A is the fast food chain that closes on Sundays and still beats every place that stays open all 7 days. That alone says everything.
The sandwich is simple but perfectly executed. Pickle-juice marinated chicken breast, breaded and fried, on a buttered brioche bun. Juicy inside, crispy outside. No mystery fillers. The Spicy Deluxe is for people with actual personality.
The service is absurdly good for fast food. They say "my pleasure" and they mean it. The drive-thru has people outside with tablets taking orders in real time, the most efficient in the industry. You feel like a customer, not a number.
The nuggets are real breast meat, no mechanically separated mystery chicken. The Waffle Fries hold their salt perfectly. The sauces, especially the Chick-fil-A Sauce and Polynesian, are reason enough to go on their own.
But the best part, and there is no debate, is the Frosted Lemonade. Freshly squeezed lemonade blended with soft-serve vanilla ice cream. Creamy, tangy, cold, and sweet all at once. No fast food drink comes close. If you walk into a Chick-fil-A and don't order the Frosted Lemonade, you basically wasted the trip.

Google review of The Dead Rabbit (4 out of 5, by Renauld “NauldoNation” Brown, 2 months ago): The Dead Rabbit was a solid stop on our trip, but for us, it didn’t quite live up to all the hype. Don’t get me wrong—it’s a good Irish bar with a great atmosphere, and the Guinness was poured well and went down easy.

One thing I did enjoy was looking over the impressive selection of Irish whiskeys displayed on the top shelves. If you’re a whiskey fan, it’s fun just seeing the variety they have behind the bar.

That said, nothing really stood out as being extraordinary. The drinks were good, the service was good, and the atmosphere was enjoyable, but at the end of the day it felt like a really good Irish pub rather than a must-see destination.

I’d still recommend stopping in if you’re in the area or want to check an iconic New York bar off your list. Just go in with realistic expectations. For us, it was a quality Irish pub with great Guinness and a fantastic whiskey selection—not necessarily a place that completely lived up to the legendary reputation.

The experience was a bit mixed, but overall still pretty good. Two people ordered the fish sandwich with fries. The fries were easily the highlight of the table, crispy and honestly the best part of multiple dishes. The fish itself got mixed reviews: one person said it was kind of lacking flavor, while the other thought it was just okay, nothing special.

Another coworker ordered the steak frites medium, but it came out much closer to rare, like, very rare. That said, it was still flavorful, and once again, the fries carried.

I ordered the chopped iceberg salad without bacon. The portion was great, but it leaned a little watery and could’ve used more seasoning to really bring it together.

Service wise, we did have to ask for silverware, but it looked like the bartender was running the show solo and pretty overwhelmed, so it didn’t feel like a huge deal.

All in all, we’d probably come back just earlier next time so we actually have a shot at that lobster special.

Google review of Stout NYC (4 out of 5, by Nia Daye, 2 months ago): While in the city last weekend, we were looking for a place to watch the FIFA match and McGregor vs. Holloway fight. Initially we walked to a couple other places not far away, but then circled back to this place which ended up being pretty for us (it was across the street from where we were staying). We got there early enough that it didn't take long to get inside and we had our pick at bar seats, so we got one right in front of the TVs that had both fifa and the fights on.

The place itself is pretty big and spacious with a long bar on the left side as you are walking through, and high top tables and booths behind it. The vibe and decor gives what you would like of a pub. But again, very spacious and it eventually filled up fast after we were there for a little while.

Service was good and our waitress (one of the bartenders) was great at checking on us, getting us what we need and just had overall good energy. We had a few rounds of shots and drinks along with our food. I got the Spicy Chicken Sandwich and opted for sweet potato fries instead of regular fries, and it was pretty good. Cooked well, tasty, the slaw was fresh and added flavor but wasn't overbearing. My boyfriend said he enjoyed his food too which was the Double Stacked Smash Burger with white cheddar and add-ons of bacon, lettuce and tomato.

Overall, good spot for food, drinks and to catch the game.

Google review of Sky Dental (5 out of 5, by Seena Alamarie, 3 months ago): Sky Dental has honestly been one of the best dental offices I’ve been to. Everyone is welcoming, and the entire office makes you feel comfortable from the moment you walk in.

Dr. Tonkian is incredibly thorough and attentive. She took her time during my initial exam and X-rays, explained everything clearly, and never made me feel rushed. She actually listens when you tell her something hurts, and you can tell she has the experience to know when something with your teeth or bite isn’t quite right. One thing I really LOVED was that she gave me breaks throughout the appointment to let me relax my jaw. I’ve never had another dentist do that before, and it made the entire experience so much easier and more comfortable.

Jessie at the front desk is also amazing. He’s always so kind, organized, and on top of everything. Whether I have questions or need help scheduling an appointment, he’s always happy to help.

It’s hard to find a dental office where you feel like people genuinely care, but that’s exactly how I felt at Sky Dental. If you’ve been putting off going to the dentist or have dental anxiety, I definitely recommend coming here.

Most importantly, modernized equipment and digital record keeping; able to explain and itemize care and service in clear, easy to understand way.

I came in for an emergency - crown cracked. Tend was the only dental care I could find on a Friday with same day service - they were able to see me within 2 hours of my incidence. On top of, assessment, care plan proposal were done within 24 hours.

It wasn't cheap but so was my last dentist. With Tend, at least I don't have to deal with murky billings and (actual) paper works.

One small winkle. When I returned second day for the temporary, I had waited over half hour after my appointment time be seen, though things went well from then on. Hence one star off.

All in all, pretty satisfied with the care and service I received so far. I will stick with Tend for the foreseeable future.

Google review of Alba Dry Cleaners & Tailoring (5 out of 5, by Vivian Ly, 5 months ago): I would actually give them a 8/5 if I could! They got a tragic pizza grease stain out of a Blueberry trench for a reasonable price.

I was carrying a pizza box home far away from my coat and at one point, I looked down and all of the grease from a closed box had poured all over my trench coat. I called seven different dry cleaners. Most were unhelpful, and threw out insane prices the moment they heard Burburry. I had a shop quote me $245 as a starting point, and tell me that there were no guarantees.

I walked into Alba, and the staff just said they would handle it and if they couldn’t get it out, I didn’t need to pay. They didn’t try to alarm me, or make things seem worse than they were like every other place. They kept it really simple, and asked if I was willing to give them a chance. I’m deeply appreciative of how quickly they got it out, how easy they made the process, and that they even delivered the coat back to my apartment for $45. I couldn’t recommend this place over and over again and will definitely be coming back.

docs.text:
Google review of Glowly (1 out of 5, by Katherine Rojas, 6 months ago): I got my nails done yesterday and I’m extremely disappointed with the quality of service, especially for the price ($158).

I had originally booked with a senior technician (which is more expensive), but my appointment was switched last minute. I was told Alice was also a senior technician, however based on my experience, she clearly did not perform at that level.

During the cuticle work, she was very rough and hurt me twice without apologizing. I had specifically booked a Russian manicure, but the proper technique did not seem to be followed (no proper hard gel leveling or hand flipping for an even finish).

The French tip design was rushed and uneven. I pointed this out while I was there and also spoke to the receptionist, but the only solution offered at the time was a pair of collagen gloves, which did not address the issue.

Less than 24 hours later, my nails have already started chipping, which is completely unacceptable for a service at this price point. There was also visible leftover white polish around my nails, showing a lack of proper cleanup and attention to detail.

I called the next day to report the chipping and was offered to have them fixed by a regular nail technician—not a senior tech, which is what I originally paid for. I was also offered a $15 credit for a future appointment, which I find inadequate given the overall experience, and I do not feel comfortable returning.

Overall, I’m very disappointed with the service, quality, and lack of appropriate resolution. I would not recommend this salon based on my experience.

docs.text:
Google review of PureGym FiDi (3 out of 5, by Tal Sela, 3 months ago): I would say this gym is honestly a solid 4 out of 5, but I am giving it 3 stars, and here is why.

If we take 5 stars as the ideal gym, the first half-star comes off for the broken showers. There are only four showers in the men’s locker room, and two of them are broken. In one of them, even the light no longer works. In my opinion, that is simply not serious.

I am also taking off one full star for the way the space is organized. For those who do not know, this gym has two floors: the first floor is a bit smaller, and the second floor is a bit bigger. The issue is that there is an unreasonable number of cardio machines. There is already a large cardio area on the second floor, but for some reason, half of the first floor is also taken up by cardio equipment.

To be clear, even during peak hours on a Monday evening, the upstairs cardio area is not completely full. The downstairs cardio area is almost never busy - usually there are just a couple of people there.

This could be fixed in a very simple way: either remove the cardio area from the first floor completely and replace it with a proper stretching area, a free weights area, kettlebells, and similar equipment, or reduce the upstairs cardio area and use that space for free weights instead.

The final half-star comes off for the free weights area. Honestly, it is not serious. This is probably the most popular area in the entire gym, yet it is squeezed into a small cramped room where it is difficult to even breathe properly. Because of that, it is constantly hot and the air feels stale. I really do not understand why this area is so poorly arranged.

To summarize: I am giving this gym 3 stars specifically because the space is badly organized. At the same time, I understand that my preferences may be specific, and maybe for the average gym user this amount of cardio equipment is fine. So objectively, the gym is probably closer to a 4. But for me personally, because of the poor layout and the free weights area, it is a 3.

UPDATE:
As of today, 3 out of 4 showers are not working - only one shower is usable.

I also would not put much trust in the owner’s response saying that repairs are supposedly planned. The reason I stopped going to the Bryant Park location was exactly this kind of situation: I waited around 8 months for the promised renovation of the lifting / squat area, and it never happened. Eventually, I had to switch to this location.

Google review of The Learning Experience - Manhattan (5 out of 5, by Merritt Thomas, 8 months ago): We couldn’t be happier with TLE - it is a wonderful nurturing environment for babies to pre-K.  TLE is impeccably run and led by a wonderful team, headed by Ms. Jessica, the director, who is on top of everything going on in the school.  Teachers are high quality - kind, attentive, and invested in the children… many have been here for years, which speaks volumes.  Communication with parents is excellent, with clear weekly emails, and daily photos that give real insight into what the children are doing and how their days are going.  The entire administration knows the names of every child, and greets them by name each morning as they walk in.

The kids are constantly engaged in creative activities - they have hands-on learning every day and are doing fun messy art projects as toddlers, and running little experiments in 3K and pre-K.  They are taken outside to run and play every day, weather-permitting.  During the year, there are high quality enrichment classes brought in to supplement the curriculum, including special science instruction, theater classes, and dance classes.  During the summer camp, there is even more - soccer instruction and magic and water Fridays etc.

Holidays are thoughtfully celebrated throughout the year and birthdays are a cause for special celebration!  The staff will help you set up decorations and teachers will throw a little party for the kids.  This is particularly great given the expense of children’s parties in Manhattan!  As a bonus, the annual “school photos” are beautifully done by a fantastic independent photographer - we use ours for our holiday card every year!

TLE is a real community for families - parents say hi to each other in the hallways and on the local playground in the evening and weekends.  It’s a very international community, which is wonderful.  TLE is just a real gem - the kind of warm loving environment you want for your child - our son has attended since he was 18 months and he is a thriving 4 year-old.  We couldn’t recommend TLE more highly.

I also spent a lot of time researching the right timing for her spay and chose to wait until after her first heat cycle. While I’m very happy with that decision, I would only recommend it to others if you have the time and attention to closely monitor every subtle change in your dog. This pet hospital has been a complete breath of fresh air and a huge source of relief throughout the entire process. From the day I brought MJ home, they’ve supported us through everything. Google review of Easy Wag FiDi (1 out of 5, by Vincent Curatolo, 3 months ago): We just got back from a three day trip and boarded our puppy Sunny here. We took him in for the temperament test and 3 required daycare stays beforehand, and seemingly we were all set to board him. He sees to be getting along totally fine with the other dogs, and we were never made aware of any issues during his first few days there.

A few days later, while on a trip, we received a lengthy text out of nowhere saying that he was “too friendly” with other dogs and wouldn’t respect other dogs’ boundaries. They proposed moving him to a pet sitter as a result, which we of course told them we were uncomfortable with. After I called them, it seemed like more of a proposal to go with the pet sitter, so we opted out of it and asked that he be kept separate if he was bothering other dogs or vice versa. Hours later we got a call from the owner, but no voicemail or text - of course we didn’t think it was urgent as a result and didn’t call back - we thought we had a resolution and were on vacation so we didn’t think there was anything urgent to discuss.

Lo and behold, the owner put him with the pet sitter, which we only found out about when we showed up 2 days later to pick him up. In prior experiences with other kennels I have never had to worry about my dog - if there was an issue, they would resolve it on their own and not bother us while we’re traveling. I understand wanting to do what’s best for all of the dogs, but I don’t understand why Easy Wag acted against our wishes and potentially put our dog in an even more uncomfortable situation. If he had been truly aggressive I would understand having done what they did, but that doesn’t seem to be the case!

On top of the miscommunication, the owner yelled and cursed at my husband for asking for a refund. If you’re a business owner you should know to respect customers and listen to them! We would have found a pet sitter on our own if we thought he couldn’t handle boarding- plus Easy Wag wouldn’t / shouldn’t have accepted him if they also didn’t think he was ready! The whole handling of this situation was just so bizarre - the girl at the front desk was super nice and reasonable but the owner is completely rude and was saying the exact opposite of what she told us about the situation!

I wish we had a better experience but I can’t recommend this business, especially for those with puppies. It should be very easy for a kennel to separate a dog if they are misbehaving or if other dogs are mistreating them. And moving a dog to another pet sitter should only be an absolutely drastic option - it clearly was unnecessary for this situation and caused so much unnecessary stress.

Google review of ZARA (4 out of 5, by Raquel Gerlani, a year ago): Great location and spacious layout, but long checkout lines

This Zara is huge—around three floors—and the layout feels modern and well-organized, especially upstairs where it’s brighter and more open  ￼. The staff seem low in number, though: the checkout area splits the space in half, and my line wound tightly through the store—felt especially cramped during a weekday lunch rush ().

👍 Pros:
•	Convenient FiDi location at 222 Broadway, Financial District  ￼
•	Three spacious floors stocked with the new seasonal collection ($20–200 range)  ￼
•	Modern design, self-checkout options, and pickup services via the app  ￼

👎 Cons:
•	Long lines at registers—especially around midday on weekdays  ￼
•	Some shoppers noted inconsistent sizing across items  ￼

📅 Hours (subject to change):
•	Mon–Tue: 10 AM – 8 PM
•	Wed–Thu: up to 9 PM
•	Sun: 10 AM – 8 PM  ￼
(Waze lists slightly varied times—Mon–Fri 9:30 AM–9 PM; Sat 10 AM–9 PM; Sun 11 AM–8 PM ().)

⸻

🛍️ Final take:

A stylish, well-stocked Zara in a super accessible spot—perfect for grabbing office-friendly pieces or weekend outfits. Just be prepared for possible wait times at checkout. If you’re quick and catch it off‑peak, it’s a solid shopping stop in FiDi!

Google review of Chase Bank (1 out of 5, by Pei Yun Chung, a year ago): It’s October 29, 2024, and I’m at the 28 Library St. Chase branch, just trying to get a five-year bank statement printed. Should be simple, right? Well, not so fast! They tell me they can’t help because – wait for it – paper is “expensive.”

Now, I’m sitting there, doing some quick mental math. You can get 300 sheets of premium A4 paper, made in the U.S., for around $20 to $30 – that’s including NYC sales tax. Meanwhile, every time I’ve transferred money from Taiwan, Chase has cost me a $50 fee for online international wires. At least ten times! So that’s over $500 in fees. But apparently, printing my statements is going to bankrupt them!

And then, as if it couldn’t get any better, they say they can only send me my statements one year at a time. One year at a time! I mean, come on – my own banking history, and they’re treating it like it’s some rare archival material. Even when I showed them Chase’s own policy, which says I could pay the fee and pick up the statements in the branch, they rejected me anyway – no reason, just a flat-out “no.”

I ask if they can show me the rules that back up these rejections – you know, just a little proof. And what do they come up with? Absolutely nothing. Then, for about 30 minutes, we’re sitting in the meeting room, where two more employees join in, like we’re about to hold a summit on the economics of paper. And guess what? Those employees just as lost as everyone else.

So, no five-year paper statement for me, but I did leave with a solid story about how a hundreds-of-billions dollar bank can’t afford paper… even with NYC sales tax.
